documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up of iron deficiency anemia after colonoscopy. Colon polyp (precancerous, high-grade dysplasia) was removed 12/2; GI wants a look at the site in about 6 months. Taking ferrous sulfate daily, dark stools expected, mild constipation managed with prunes. Energy noticeably better, walks his neighborhood loop again. Weight steady. No bleeding. Breathing at baseline, voice normal.

Exam: less pale. Lungs diminished, no stridor. Heart regular. Abdomen benign.

CBC today.

A/P
- Iron deficiency anemia, improving on oral iron; continue. Heme visit in May.
- Colon adenoma: surveillance colonoscopy around June, reminded him.
- HTN on lisinopril/HCTZ, home BPs 130s.
- Emphysema stable.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sean, hemoglobin is up to 11.8 from 9.2. The iron is working. Keep taking it until the hematology visit.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at his kitchen table, wife beside him.

Cough since early February, bringing up yellowish phlegm most mornings. No fever, no blood, no chest pain. Breathing maybe slightly worse; using albuterol a bit more. Not smoking. Eating fine but jeans looser.

Looks comfortable on video, speaking in full sentences, no audible stridor, voice normal.

A/P: 6 weeks of productive cough in severe emphysema, ex-smoker. Chest x-ray, walk-in at the imaging center any day this week. Not prescribing antibiotics without fever or a change on imaging. Will call with the result.

documents.body: Chest x-ray ordered 3/24 not yet done. LVM reminding pt to walk in to imaging.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Hyperexpanded lungs consistent with emphysema. A mass is present in the right lower lobe. No pneumothorax. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Tracheal air column unremarkable.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit: 5/5/2025

Mr. Hennessey returns for follow-up of iron deficiency anemia (ascending colon adenoma removed in December). The anemia has corrected on oral iron. New since his last visit is a cough, now about three months, bringing up yellowish sputum, and further weight loss. No fevers, no night sweats, no blood in the sputum.

Vitals: BP 145/90, pulse 88, respirations 18.
Exam: breath sounds reduced at the right base with dullness to percussion there. No adenopathy.

Labs today: hemoglobin 13.5, WBC 7,500, platelets 250,000, sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.0, fasting glucose 100.

Chest radiograph today: mass in the right lower lobe.

Assessment:
1. Right lower lobe lung mass in a former heavy smoker; malignancy until proven otherwise.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, resolved. Continue ferrous sulfate for now.

Plan: referral to pulmonology for bronchoscopy with biopsy, requested urgently. We will see him again once tissue is back.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Lung mass
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Heme/onc called me directly re: RLL mass on yesterday's CXR, bronchoscopy being set up. I called Sean and his wife. Frightened but composed. Told him we'd stay close through all of this; visit with me after the biopsy.

conditions.label: Non-small cell lung cancer, right lower lobe

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
A. Right lower lobe endobronchial mass, forceps biopsies: non-small cell carcinoma, squamous cell type (p40 positive, TTF-1 negative).
B. Lymph node, station 4L, EBUS-guided needle aspiration: metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
C. Lymph node, station 4R, EBUS-guided needle aspiration: metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
D. Lymph node, station 7, EBUS-guided needle aspiration: benign lymphoid tissue, no malignancy.
Molecular testing sent separately.
reports.conclusion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the right lower lobe, non-small cell type, with metastasis to station 4R and contralateral station 4L lymph nodes.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with EBUS
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
FLEXIBLE BRONCHOSCOPY WITH ENDOBRONCHIAL ULTRASOUND
Date: 5/19/2025
Indication: right lower lobe mass.
Anesthesia: general, laryngeal mask airway.

Findings: vocal cords move normally. Trachea: the prior papilloma resection site in the mid trachea is smooth with no recurrent lesion. Carina sharp. Left bronchial tree normal. Right lower lobe: friable endobronchial tumor partly occluding the basal segments; forceps biopsies taken.
EBUS: stations 4R, 4L and 7 sampled by needle aspiration.

Complications: none. Discharged home the same day.

Pulmonary & Critical Care

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Lung Cancer Diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his wife after the biopsy showed squamous cell lung cancer in the right lower lobe with cancer in lymph nodes on both sides of the chest (EBUS 4R and 4L). PET-CT is tomorrow, brain MRI Thursday, thoracic oncology next Monday.

He wanted to know whether quitting in 2022 had been for nothing; told him it wasn't, it's helped his heart, legs and lungs and will help him get through treatment. His father died of lung cancer at 60 and he keeps coming back to that. Sleeping poorly the last week. Not depressed by screen; worried, which is fair.

Cough continues, some yellow sputum, no blood. Breathing at baseline.

Exam: tired but well. Lungs diminished, reduced at R base. Heart regular. No edema.

Meds reconciled: HCTZ 25, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 daily.

Advance care planning (35 min with patient and wife): health care proxy on file, wife is agent, he confirms. He wants all treatment the oncologists recommend. Not ready to talk about what he'd want if treatment stops working; open to it later. MOLST not completed today.

A/P
- NSCLC, squamous, RLL with mediastinal nodes. Staging underway. I'll coordinate and see him between oncology visits.
- Everything else stable, no changes.

conditions.label: Non-small cell lung cancer, right lower lobe

documents.title: Thoracic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT
Date: June 2, 2025

Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma of the right lower lobe.

Staging:
- PET-CT 5/28/2025: 4.6 cm FDG-avid right lower lobe mass; FDG-avid right hilar and bilateral mediastinal lymph nodes; no distant metastatic disease. No pleural effusion.
- MRI brain with and without contrast 5/29/2025: no intracranial metastasis.
- EBUS 5/19: 4R and 4L positive, station 7 negative.
- Molecular: no EGFR, ALK or ROS1 alteration.
Stage: T2b N3 M0, stage IIIB. Not a surgical candidate.

Performance status: ECOG 1.
Comorbidities noted: severe emphysema, hypertension, PAD with femoral stent, right renal artery stenosis, prior tracheal papilloma and colon adenoma.

Recommendation, discussed at length with Mr. Hennessey and his wife: definitive concurrent chemoradiation with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel and thoracic radiation to 60 Gy in 30 fractions, followed by consolidation durvalumab for up to a year. Simulation with radiation oncology this week; planned start 6/9.

Oncology

documents.title: Oncology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thoracic oncology letter in: stage IIIB squamous NSCLC, T2b N3 M0, no driver mutation, no brain mets. Chemoradiation starting 6/9, then durvalumab. Problem list updated. Asked RN to set a check-in call mid-treatment.

medications.sig: AUC 2 IV weekly with radiation (cancer center)
45 mg/m2 IV weekly with radiation (cancer center)

documents.title: Mid-treatment check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt, week 4 of chemoradiation. Tired, as expected. No fever. Breathing ok. Wife driving him daily. Nothing needed from us; reminded him we're here.

documents.title: Radiation Oncology Treatment Summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY TREATMENT SUMMARY

Diagnosis: stage IIIB (T2b N3 M0) squamous cell carcinoma, right lower lobe.
Treatment: 6/9/2025 - 7/18/2025. Right lower lobe primary, right hilar and bilateral mediastinal nodes, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, IMRT, with concurrent weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel by medical oncology.

Tolerance: completed as planned with no treatment breaks.

Follow-up: medical oncology to begin consolidation durvalumab; radiation oncology follow-up with imaging in 3 months.

Radiation Oncology

documents.title: Medication question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called: oncology nurse asked whether he should keep taking the iron and baby aspirin during chemo. Reviewed with PCP: continue both unless oncology says otherwise, take the iron at a different time from other pills. Wife satisfied.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three weeks out from finishing chemoradiation (last fraction 7/18). Still tired by mid-afternoon, naps. Appetite coming back slowly; down to 79 kg. Cough less, sputum clear now. Using albuterol a few times a week. Durvalumab infusions to start later this month.

BP 132/80. Lungs diminished, fewer sounds R base. Skin over the radiation field intact. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
- Stage IIIB NSCLC, completed chemoRT. Durvalumab next per oncology.
- Anemia: Hgb 12.6 after chemo, ferritin 88 so iron stores are fine. Stop the ferrous sulfate.
- HTN: on target. Same regimen.
- Weight: protein shakes, small frequent meals.
- Colon surveillance scope: was due in June, put off during treatment; GI will reschedule with oncology's input.
- Flu and COVID shots in the fall if oncology agrees.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, blood count is 12.6, a little low from the chemo but fine, and your iron stores are full, so you can stop the iron pill. Kidney numbers are normal.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
On durvalumab every 4 weeks since 8/25 (two infusions so far); we didn't have that on his list until today. Tolerating it: no rash, no diarrhea, no new cough. Energy better than in August. Eating more, weight stable at 78. Walking twice a day.

BP fine. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Heart regular. Skin clear. No edema.

A/P
- NSCLC on consolidation durvalumab; added to med list.
- HTN, PAD, renal artery stenosis: stable on current meds.
- Emphysema: at baseline.
- Flu and updated COVID vaccine today, oncology OK'd by message.
- RTC 3 months.

reports.text:
CT ANGIOGRAPHY ABDOMEN
Indication: abdominal pain, pulsatile abdominal mass.
Technique: arterial and venous phase imaging after IV contrast with multiplanar reconstructions.
Findings: Saccular aneurysm arising from the proximal superior mesenteric artery just distal to its origin from the aorta, measuring 3.8 cm in maximal diameter, projecting posteriorly. No surrounding hematoma or extravasation. The SMA beyond the aneurysm opacifies normally. Celiac axis and inferior mesenteric artery patent. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys unremarkable apart from known renal arteries. Bowel normal in caliber without wall thickening. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: 3.8 cm saccular aneurysm of the proximal superior mesenteric artery, projecting posteriorly. No rupture.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Arrival 11/12/2025 11:40

Chief complaint: abdominal pain.

HPI: 58-year-old man with stage IIIB lung cancer on immunotherapy. For about three months he has had a dull, vague abdominal ache that comes and goes, more likely after he eats, sometimes going through to his back. No nausea, vomiting or diarrhea; no blood in the stool. His wife also points out that his face and neck have looked puffy for about a week.

Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, albuterol, durvalumab.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: in no distress. Face and neck appear full, neck veins distended. Lungs diminished. Abdomen: a pulsatile mass is felt in the central abdomen; it is not tender. Bowel sounds normal. No guarding.

CTA abdomen: 3.8 cm saccular proximal SMA aneurysm projecting posteriorly, no rupture.
CT chest: SVC narrowed by enlarging right paratracheal nodal tissue.

ED course: hemodynamically stable. Vascular surgery and interventional radiology consulted. Admitted to medicine.

Disposition: admitted.

conditions.label: Superior vena cava syndrome secondary to lung cancer

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST
Indication: facial swelling, known right lower lobe lung cancer after chemoradiation.
Findings: Enlarging soft tissue in the right paratracheal region compared with the staging study, consistent with nodal disease, narrowing the superior vena cava. Treated right lower lobe mass with post-radiation change. Emphysema. No pleural effusion. Prior tracheal resection site unremarkable; trachea patent.
reports.conclusion: Superior vena cava narrowing from enlarging right paratracheal nodal disease.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 11/12/2025  Discharged: 11/15/2025

Principal diagnoses:
1. Superior vena cava syndrome due to progression of stage IIIB squamous NSCLC (right paratracheal nodes).
2. Saccular aneurysm of the proximal superior mesenteric artery, 3.8 cm, symptomatic.

Course:
Admitted from the ED. CT chest showed the SVC narrowed by enlarging right paratracheal nodal disease, explaining a week of facial and neck swelling. Interventional radiology placed an SVC stent on 11/13 through the right femoral vein without complication; swelling largely resolved by the next morning.
Vascular surgery evaluated the SMA aneurysm. Given its size and his symptoms they recommend elective endovascular repair after he recovers from this admission, to be scheduled in their clinic.
Oncology saw him in hospital: this represents progression on durvalumab, which is stopped. Second-line therapy to be discussed in clinic.

Discharge medications: unchanged home medications (lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium, albuterol). Durvalumab discontinued.

Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks; oncology 11/20; vascular surgery 12/3.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Discharge summary received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary and ED record from 11/12-11/15 finally scanned. Matches what we pieced together from his wife and the visit. Problem list current.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's wife called: he's been in the hospital since Wed. Went in for the belly pain, they found an aneurysm on an intestinal artery, and also the cancer is pressing on the big vein in his chest, which is why his face was swollen. They put a stent in the vein yesterday and the swelling is much better. Expected home tomorrow. Booked post-hospital visit 11/24 with PCP. Will request records.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Spoke with wife by phone 11/14; discharge papers she brought reviewed today (summary not yet received from the hospital).

Hospitalized 11/12-11/15. Abdominal pain led to a CT showing a 3.8 cm aneurysm of the superior mesenteric artery. Also found SVC syndrome from growing lymph nodes in the chest; SVC stent 11/13. Oncology says the cancer has progressed and has stopped durvalumab; they're discussing next treatment at his 11/20 visit (he says chemo every 3 weeks starting in December). Vascular plans a stent-graft repair of the aneurysm, consult 12/3.

Now: face and neck back to normal. Still a mild ache after meals, no worse. Bowels normal, no blood. Breathing at baseline.

Exam: no facial or arm swelling, neck veins flat, R groin access site healed. Lungs diminished. Abdomen soft, pulsatile midline mass, nontender. No edema.

Meds reconciled: durvalumab off. Others unchanged.

A/P
- SVC syndrome, stented, resolved.
- SMA aneurysm, symptomatic, repair planned by vascular. Return precautions for severe or sudden pain.
- NSCLC with nodal progression; second-line therapy per oncology.
- HTN, renal artery stenosis: BMP today.
- Will see him again before the repair.

documents.title: January
documents.author: patient
documents.body: vascular set the artery repair for jan 21. should I still come see you in january?

documents.title: RE: January
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, please keep the January 12 visit so we can go over everything before the repair. Bring the list of the new chemo medicines if they gave you one.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Started docetaxel every 3 weeks on 12/8, two cycles so far; adding it to his list now. Tired for a few days after each infusion. No fevers. Vascular repair of the SMA aneurysm booked for 1/21, endovascular through the groin; they told him to stay on aspirin.

Abdominal ache after meals continues, same as before, no weight loss beyond what we know. Face/neck swelling has not come back.

Exam: weight 77. Lungs diminished. Abdomen soft, nontender, pulsatile mass. No edema.

A/P
- NSCLC on docetaxel; CBC today at oncology's request (shared).
- SMA aneurysm, repair 1/21. Nothing to change on our side.
- HTN controlled.

documents.title: home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Home since yesterday. They put the covered stent in the belly artery wednesday, stayed one night. groin is a little sore. they said no lifting for a week. do I need to see you?

documents.title: RE: home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it went smoothly. No need to come in unless the groin swells, bleeds, or you get belly pain, fever or numbness in the leg; then call right away. We'll see you as planned next month. Can you ask the vascular office to send us their procedure note?

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One month after endovascular repair of the SMA aneurysm (1/21, one night in hospital). The after-meal belly pain is gone, first time in months. Groin healed. Vascular sees him with a CT in March. We still have no operative note.

Docetaxel continues every 3 weeks; tired for a few days after each one, then OK. Appetite fair. Not smoking.

Exam: Lungs diminished. Abdomen soft, nontender, no pulsatile mass felt. R groin healed, no hematoma or bruit. Pedal pulses present.

A/P
- SMA aneurysm s/p covered stent, asymptomatic.
- NSCLC on second-line docetaxel.
- HTN/RAS: BMP today; contrast twice this winter.
- RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Requested operative note from vascular surgery for 1/21 procedure. Third request for this item.

reports.text:
CT ANGIOGRAPHY ABDOMEN
Indication: follow-up after endovascular repair of SMA aneurysm.
Findings: Covered stent in the proximal superior mesenteric artery is patent with normal distal opacification. The aneurysm sac is excluded with no contrast filling it and no endoleak. Celiac and inferior mesenteric arteries patent. Aorta normal caliber. No new abdominal findings.
reports.conclusion: Patent SMA stent graft. Aneurysm excluded, no endoleak.

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Follow-up
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY CLINIC
Date: 3/9/2026

Seen seven weeks after endovascular exclusion of a 3.8 cm saccular proximal SMA aneurysm with a covered stent (1/21/2026). Postprandial pain has resolved. Access site healed.

CTA today: stent graft patent, aneurysm excluded, no endoleak.

Plan: continue aspirin 81 mg indefinitely. Repeat CTA in 12 months. Return sooner for any abdominal pain.

Of note, he also has a left femoral artery stent from 2021 placed by our group; he walks without claudication and pedal pulses are present.

Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Records follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Vascular follow-up letter and CTA from 3/9 received and scanned. Operative note for 1/21 still outstanding; vascular office says it is in their system but would not fax it without another release. Release mailed to patient.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST
Indication: new seizure, lung cancer.
Findings: Multiple well-circumscribed enhancing lesions located at the gray-white matter junction, each with surrounding vasogenic edema. No hemorrhage. No midline shift. Ventricles normal in size. No acute infarct. Major intracranial flow voids preserved.
reports.conclusion: Multiple well-circumscribed lesions at the gray-white junction with vasogenic edema, consistent with metastases.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Arrival 5/2/2026 07:50 by ambulance.

Chief complaint: seizure.

HPI: 59-year-old man with stage IIIB squamous NSCLC on docetaxel and a history of SVC syndrome (stented). His wife found him having a seizure in bed this morning. No prior seizures. She says he has complained of a headache for two weeks that over-the-counter pain relievers have not touched, and that he has been forgetting things and groping for words in conversation.

Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, albuterol, docetaxel.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vital signs stable. Drowsy and slow to answer, consistent with the postictal state; oriented by the end of his stay here. No focal neurologic deficit: pupils equal and reactive, face symmetric, strength and sensation equal, no drift. Tongue without laceration.

MRI brain: multiple well-circumscribed lesions at the gray-white junction with vasogenic edema, consistent with metastases.

ED course: levetiracetam load, dexamethasone. No further seizure. Admitted to medicine with neuro-oncology and radiation oncology consults.

Emergency Medicine

Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily, then taper per oncology schedule

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 5/2/2026, discharged 5/5/2026.

Diagnoses: metastatic squamous cell lung carcinoma to brain, multiple lesions with vasogenic edema; new-onset seizure.

Hospital course: started levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily and dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily. No further seizures. Headache improved by day 2 and word-finding was better on discharge. Radiation oncology recommends stereotactic radiosurgery, simulation done, treatment 5/14. Medical oncology to continue docetaxel after radiosurgery.

Discharge medications: levetiracetam 500 mg BID (new); dexamethasone 4 mg BID with taper to be directed by radiation oncology (new); lisinopril 20 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily; tiotropium; albuterol as needed.

Instructions: no driving; seizure precautions; call for any further seizure.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; radiation oncology 5/14; medical oncology 5/19.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Hospital notification
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Notified by hospital admission feed: pt admitted 5/2 with seizure. Called wife: brain spots found, he's more himself today, home likely tomorrow. TCM visit booked 5/11.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. Discharge summary reviewed (received 5/7).

Admitted 5/2-5/5 after a first seizure at home; MRI showed several brain metastases with swelling. On levetiracetam 500 BID and dexamethasone 4 BID. Radiosurgery Thursday 5/14.

Since home: no further seizures. Headache much less. Wife says his words are coming easier; he agrees, still loses a word now and then. No falls. Not driving; we discussed that Massachusetts requires 6 months seizure-free before he drives again, and his wife will drive.

Exam: alert, conversational, mild word-finding pauses. No focal weakness, gait steady. Lungs diminished. No edema.

A/P
- Brain metastases with seizure. Levetiracetam continued; dexamethasone taper per radiation oncology. Checking glucose and potassium on the steroid.
- NSCLC: docetaxel to resume after SRS.
- Goals: he wants to keep treating. Offered to revisit planning conversation from last year at the next visit, wife grateful.
- Seizure precautions reviewed: no driving, no ladders, showers rather than baths.

documents.title: Radiosurgery Treatment Note
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY

Stereotactic radiosurgery delivered 5/14/2026 to the brain metastases identified on MRI 5/2/2026, single fraction, frameless mask immobilization. Treatment was well tolerated without acute side effects.

Plan: dexamethasone taper over 3 weeks per the attached schedule. Levetiracetam to continue. Follow-up MRI brain in 3 months (mid-August). Medical oncology resumes systemic therapy.

Radiation Oncology
